items.title: U.S. and Iran Survey the Damage After a Night of Intense Strikes
items.summary: The American military said its barrage was retaliation against recent attacks on U.S. forces and marine traffic. Iranian officials said a wedding was hit and civilians killed.

items.title: The ‘Miracle House’ That Survived Nepal’s Floods
items.summary: People are coming to take photos of the green-painted house, which kept the Pyakurel family safe as the area all around them was destroyed by rampaging floodwaters.

items.title: Attacks in Black Sea Threaten to Strangle Global Grain Supply
items.summary: Strikes on ports and vessels by both Russia and Ukraine have left farmers facing ruin and could cause another worldwide food shock.

items.title: Inside the Fight Against a Flesh-Eating Fly in Mexico
items.summary: For the first time in a year, the U.S.-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle imports following a screwworm infestation across the region. The battle against the flesh-eating fly has only just begun deep in Mexico.

items.title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Docks in Thailand, Giving Weary Crew a Break
items.summary: Thousands of sailors and Marines serve on the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln, which came into the spotlight because of a tough deployment in the war in Iran.

items.title: Status of Iran’s Nuclear Program Is Unclear, U.N. Watchdog Says
items.summary: As the war sputters on, an internal report from the International Atomic Energy Agency said Iran’s refusal to grant access to its inspectors was an urgent concern.

items.title: Hong Kong Pro-Democracy Activist Joshua Wong Pleads Guilty to Collusion
items.summary: The pro-democracy dissident was accused of urging Western politicians like Nancy Pelosi and Marco Rubio to pressure Hong Kong by imposing sanctions on the city.

items.title: Netanyahu’s Israel Is Looking for a Fight in Every Direction
items.summary: The Israeli leader, facing a tough re-election contest, may need a security crisis to rally voters behind him and hold on to his job.

items.title: Do Active Shooter Drills Help? Two Asian Nations Grapple With Gun Violence.
items.summary: After school shootings, Thailand and the Philippines are taking different approaches to the drills, which are common practice in the United States.

items.title: After the Earthquake, They Used A.I. to Mobilize Aid
items.summary: As volunteers struggled to get supplies to quake victims in Colombia, a few tech workers built an app to map and organize the sprawling relief effort.

items.title: Uber and Wayve to Start Testing Robotaxis in London
items.summary: Uber and the British start-up Wayve are the latest to start testing autonomous cars in one of the world’s largest markets for ride-hailing services.

items.title: Southwest to Open Premium Airport Lounges Across the Country
items.summary: The airline said that lounges in Baltimore, Honolulu, Nashville and Austin, Texas, would debut starting late next year, and that seven more were in the works.

items.title: Trump’s Tactics to Lower Beef Prices and Appease Ranchers Fall Short
items.summary: The Agriculture Department offered new initiatives for ranchers after President Trump said he would import more beef. The moves aren’t a quick fix.

items.title: Chevron Expansion in Venezuela Extends U.S. Influence Over Oil Riches
items.summary: The U.S. energy giant, which stayed in the country after other Western companies left, will invest $7 billion in the country to more than double its production there.

items.title: Investors Still on Edge Over War, Debt and Inflation
items.summary: U.S. and Iranian forces traded attacks again, pushing oil prices higher, stocks lower and making bond investors nervous.

items.title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
items.summary: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.

items.title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?
items.summary: If you own bonds, they may be in a broad fund that hasn’t lost much money. And that fund may do much better in the next several years.

items.title: FiveThirtyEight’s Podcast Hosts Reunite for a New Show
items.summary: Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke will host “Still Counting,” a nonpartisan politics show — on a decidedly partisan podcast network.

items.title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years
items.summary: The magazine, famous for publishing Jack London stories and Norman Rockwell art, will continue online.

items.title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
items.summary: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.

items.title: In a Big Win, Google Won’t Have to Break Up Its Ad Tech Business, Court Rules
items.summary: In a long-awaited decision, a federal judge said Google must change its ad tech business to address antitrust issues, but did not disclose the measures.

items.title: Justice Dept. Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Suit
items.summary: The department argued in a court filing that OpenAI legally used articles by The New York Times to develop A.I., adding that national security depended on American tech dominance.

items.title: Uber Lays Off 10% of Employees in Sweeping Reorganization
items.summary: The layoffs affect about 3,300 workers, as Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi bets on a “leaner organization.”

items.title: Noise and Motion Monitors in Their Homes? These Tenants Say No.
items.summary: The public housing authority in Concord, N.H., installed monitoring devices in 300 homes. Tenants are now suing to remove the Minut sensors.

items.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
items.summary: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.

items.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
items.summary: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.

items.title: Map Apps Are Handling Trump’s Renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America Differently
items.summary: Navigation companies face a new dilemma after President Trump ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed Lake America.

items.title: John Ternus Replaces Tim Cook as Apple CEO
items.summary: Big technology and management changes are greeting John Ternus, whose long-serving predecessor, Tim Cook, will stay on as executive chair.

items.title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
items.summary: Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced more than a million advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.
